~~~python~~~
import pandas as pd

# Create the dataframe
data = {
    'year': [1998, 1999, 2001, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2009, 2012, 2013],
    'competition': ['world junior championships', 'european junior championships', 'european u23 championships', 'universiade', 'world championships', 'european championships', 'olympic games', 'world championships', 'olympic games', 'world championships'],
    'venue': ['annecy , france', 'riga , latvia', 'amsterdam , netherlands', 'daegu , south korea', 'helsinki , finland', 'gothenburg , sweden', 'beijing , pr china', 'berlin , germany', 'london , great britain', 'moscow , russia'],
    'position': ['10th', '5th', '11th', '4th', '14th', '15th', '29th', '14th', '6th', '3rd'],
    'notes': ['61.51 m', '64.20 m', '66.41 m', '71.26 m', '74.53 m', '73.77 m', '70.56 m', '74.47 m', '77.17 m', '79.36 m']
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Extract numeric distance from notes column
df['distance'] = df['notes'].str.extract(r'(\d+\.\d+)').astype(float)

# Sort by year to ensure chronological order
df = df.sort_values('year')

# Get the last two competitions based on year
last_two = df.tail(2)

# Calculate average distance of last two competitions
average_distance = last_two['distance'].mean()

# Check if average distance equals 78.27
answer = (average_distance == 78.27)
